# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-9 (Extended v94)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 3, dual settings)**: (1) Paris, le Petit-Picpus convent district—Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary within walled convent garden; (2) English harbor towns and provincial areas (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Torton) with multiple named inhabitants engaged in ordinary seasonal activities. Key historical dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont); 1817 (young Parisians' excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest, trial sequence in Arras, Valjean's self-revelation, Fantine's death, Valjean's escape)**; **December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier; December 26 return to Paris)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed); **Summer Year 2 (achieved sanctuary in convent)**; **Winter Year 2 (Mother Crucifixion died, funeral, vault burial)**; **Spring Year 3 (currently occurring, approximately eight or nine years after Part Two events)**.

## Primary Locations

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved rut-filled roads. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (convent carriage gate)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above 18-foot wall. **Convent complex—three buildings**: (1) **Great Convent** (Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy, heavily shuttered); (2) **Boarding-school** (scholar lodging); (3) **Little Convent** (aged nuns of various orders, destroyed in Revolution). **Interior garden**: Vast oblong with poplar alley, forest trees, gnarled fruit-tree, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass, green mould. **Parlor (Great Convent)**: Monstrous iron lattice with black shutters (always closed). **Chapel**: Window visible from garden; nuns perform prayer/reparation. **Burial location**: Mother Crucifixion's vault beneath grand altar (concealed, no government suspicion). **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient burial ground with special Prefecture Permission for nightfall interments.

**PARISIAN BANLIEUE**: Philosophical study of suburb—amphibious zone where trees/roofs, grass/pavements, furrows/shops, divine murmur/human uproar intersect.

**ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Multiple named locations (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Torton) with ordinary inhabitants engaged in seasonal work (mill operations, baking, salt trading, farming). **Recent weather/seasonal conditions**: River up in spring (recurring pattern); frost silvered hedges; bees hummed in lavender; children chased hoops; rain threatened but held off; wind off water with salt/tar smell; light went early; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields. **Social movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead, settled Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged.

**GORBEAU HOVEL (50-52)**: Salpêtrière district, outskirts Paris. Eternally posted "Chambers to let"; presently inhabited by numerous indigent individuals (no connection to each other) from class separating from lowest petty bourgeoisie down to sewer-men and rag-pickers. **Current tenant—Jondrette family**: Father stated name "Jondrette" upon hiring chamber; entrance resembled "entrance of nothing at all"; instructed portress-stair-sweeper to respond affirmatively if inquired for Pole, Italian, or Spaniard.

**PARISIAN STREETS AND DISTRICTS**: Boulevard du Temple, Château-d'Eau regions; Rue Boucherat, Rue de Normandie, Rue de Saintonge; streets near Temple (named after French provinces under Louis XIV; now some streets named after European capitals); Pont-Neuf; Gorbeau house accessible via quays, bridges, suburbs from central Paris.

## Jean Valjean's Psychological and Spiritual Development

**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank; demonstrated gloomy talent—understood contracting to fit diameter; could economize breath for hours without dying; possessed composure and coolness contagious to others.

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works in garden daily; formerly pruner of trees; knows agricultural secrets; budded ungrafted orchard trees producing excellent fruit. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running/playing; distinguishes her laugh.

**SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION**: During night meditations rose to listen to grateful song of innocent nuns; blood ran cold—justly chastised raised voices only in blasphemy while he, wretch, had shaken fist at God. Realized: scaling wall made to escape other place of expiation now served entrance to this one. Was this symbol of his destiny? Pride vanished. Scrutinized own heart; felt pettiness; wept many times. All entering life last six months led back towards Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Sometimes at eventide knelt in middle of walk skirting chapel, prostrated in prayer. Everything surrounding him—peaceful garden, fragrant flowers, children's joyous cries, grave and simple women, silent cloister—slowly permeated him. Soul became compounded of silence, perfume, simplicity, joy. Reflected: two houses of God received him at critical moments—first when all doors closed (society rejected him); second when society pursued him (galleys yawning). Without first, relapsed into crime; without second, into torment.

## Cosette's Integration and Development

**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Unhappiness trained her to silence. Suffered much; feared everything, even to speak/breathe. Hardly begun regaining confidence since with Jean Valjean.

**CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed; only regretted Catherine but dared not say so. Once told Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself his daughter. Became convent scholar; received pupil garb. Valjean succeeded getting nuns restore mourning suit from Thénardier departure; locked up these garments plus stockings/shoes with camphor/aromatics in little valise; procured valise, set on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Current Status

**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821 or earlier) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour traversing short distances; complains aching back as usual.

**EXECUTION OF PLANS**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket, left with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert. Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery. At cemetery, Father Mestienne (grave-digger) dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Grave-digger lost card. Fauchelevent found card, buried corpse, filled grave himself.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives good wine. Old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally/protector. Nuns do not suspect him; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit and Investigation Status

**REASSIGNMENT AND REACTIVATION**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), Javert attached to Paris police. Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence.

**REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **Escape from Mouffetard**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS** (Spring Year 3): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades.

## Parisian Street Children (Gamins): Character and Significance

**GENERAL CHARACTER**: Not devoid literary intuition but lacking classic taste; not very academic. Being that bawls, scoffs, ridicules, fights; has rags like baby, tatters like philosopher; fishes sewers, hunts cesspools, extracts mirth from foulness; whips up squares with wit, grins and bites, whistles, sings, shouts, shrieks; found without seeking; Spartan to point of thieving, mad to wisdom, lyrical to filth; would crouch on Olympus yet wallows in dunghill emerging covered with stars. Gamin of Paris is Rabelais in youth. Not easily astonished/terrified; makes songs on superstitions, takes wind out of exaggerations, twits mysteries, thrusts tongue at ghosts.

**DESIRES AND ASPIRATIONS**: Two things he plays Tantalus: to overthrow government and get his trousers sewed up.

**POLICE KNOWLEDGE**: Gamin possesses all Paris policemen, can name-to-face any; studies habits, has special notes on each; reads souls like open book.

**HISTORICAL LINEAGE**: Something of that boy in Poquelin; Beaumarchais had something of it. Gaminerie is shade of Gallic spirit. Mingled with good sense, sometimes adds force, as alcohol does wine. Voltaire plays gamin. Camille Desmoulins native of faubourgs. Championnet rose from Paris pavements.

**TRANSFORMATION CAPACITY**: Respectful, ironical, insolent. Villainous teeth (badly fed); handsome eyes (wit). Would hop up paradise steps on one foot before Jehovah. All beliefs possible. Plays in gutter, straightens himself with revolt; effrontery persists before grape-shot; was scapegrace, is hero; shakes skin from lion like little Theban; Barra drummer-boy was gamin of Paris; passed from small brat to giant.

**REVOLUTIONARY POTENTIAL**: All generous social irradiations spring from science, letters, arts, education. Make men. Give them light that they may warm you. Sooner or later universal education will present itself with irresistible authority; those governing under French idea superintendence must choose: children of France or gamins of Paris; flames in light or will-o'-the-wisps in gloom.

## The Merry Barefoot Boy and Jondrette Family

**THE BOY**: Eleven or twelve years old, realized gamin ideal except for absolutely sombre and empty heart. Clothed in man's trousers (not father's) and woman's chemise (not mother's) out of charity. Has father and mother: father does not think of him, mother does not love him. Boisterous, pallid, nimble, wide-awake, jeering, with vivacious but sickly air. Goes and came, sang, played hopscotch, scraped gutters, stole little; like cats and sparrows, gayly laughed when called rogue, got angry when called thief. No shelter, no bread, no fire, no love; merry because free.

**OCCASIONAL VISITS**: Every two or three months says "Come, I'll go and see mamma!" Quitted boulevard, Cirque, Porte Saint-Martin; descended to quays, crossed bridges, reached suburbs, arrived Salpêtrière at Gorbeau hovel (50-52—"acquainted" to reader). Found distress, what sadder, no smile; cold hearth and cold hearts. Asked "Whence come you?" Replied "From the street." Asked "Whither going?" Replied "Into streets." Mother asked: "What did you come here for?"

**JONDRETTE FAMILY**: Father hired chamber in Gorbeau hovel, stated name "Jondrette"; moving in resembled "entrance of nothing at all" (principal tenant's expression); told portress-stair-sweeper "Mother So-and-So, if any one should chance inquire for a Pole or Italian, or even a Spaniard, perchance, it is I."

## M. Gillenormand and His World

**IDENTITY AND MEMORY**: Worthy man; ancient inhabitants of Rue Boucherat, Rue de Normandie, Rue de Saintonge preserve his memory, mention with complaisance. Silhouette not yet entirely disappeared from labyrinth of streets near Temple (where streets named after French provinces under Louis XIV).

**PHILOSOPHY AND HABITS**: Uttered frequently "the sensible man" and "nature." Gave nature his own acceptation in chimney-corner satires: "Nature gives civilization specimens of amusing barbarism. Europe possesses Asia and Africa on small scale. Cat is drawing-room tiger, lizard pocket crocodile. Dancers at opera are pink female savages. Do not eat men, crunch them; transform into oysters and swallow. Caribbeans leave bones, shells. Such are morals. We do not devour, we gnaw; do not exterminate, claw."

**BOYHOOD HONORS**: Took prizes at College of Moulins (birthplace); crowned by hand of Duc de Nivernais (whom he called Duc de Nevers). Neither Convention, death of Louis XVI, Napoleon, Bourbon return, nor anything erased this memory. Duc was great figure of century. "What charming grand seigneur and fine air with blue ribbon!"

**PECULIAR HABITS**: On abandoning society, immured himself in habits. Principal invariable one: kept door absolutely closed during day, never received anyone except evening. Dined at five o'clock; after that door open. "Day is vulgar, deserves only closed shutter. Fashionable people only light up minds when zenith lights stars." Barricaded against everyone, even king. Antiquated elegance of his day.

**TWO DAUGHTERS**: Came into world ten years apart; in youth bore little resemblance to each other in character/countenance; as little like sisters as possible. **Youngest**: Charming soul turned towards light, occupied with flowers, verses, music, fluttered into glorious space, enthusiastic, ethereal; wedded from youth in ideal to vague and heroic figure. **Eldest**: Espied in azure wealthy purveyor, contractor, splendidly stupid husband, million-made man, or prefect; Prefecture receptions, usher with chain, official balls, town-hall harangues, being "Madame la Préfète"—whirlwind in imagination. Both strayed in own dreams as young girls. Both had wings—one like angel, other like goose.

## Narrative Themes and Authorial Commentary

**AUDACITY AND REVOLUTION**: All sublime conquests are prizes of daring. For Revolution to take place, insufficient that Montesquieu foresee, Diderot preach, Beaumarchais announce, Condorcet calculate, Arouet prepare, Rousseau premeditate; necessary that Danton dare. Cry "Audacity!" is "Fiat lux." Necessary for forward march that proud lessons of courage permanently on heights. Daring deeds dazzle history, one of man's great sources of light. Attempt, brave, persist, persevere, be faithful to self, grasp fate bodily, astound catastrophe, affront unjust power, insult drunken victory, hold position, stand ground—that is example nations need, light electrifying them.
